events.event_narrative: Chaser reported 1.25 inch hail.
Spotter reported one-inch hail.
Local Law Enforcement reported one-inch hail.

Photo evidence of a tornado associated with the occlusion of the circulation south of the earlier bent county tornadic circulation. tornado lasted approximately 5 minutes, starting at 5:43 pm mdt, as viewed by multiple individuals looking west, to the south of Wiley, CO.

Initial updrafts of developing thunderstorms interacted with an outflow boundary and produced a landspout tornado, which was on the ground for approximately 10-15 mins. Numerous photos on social media showed a dusty landspout. This preceded the development of a mesocyclonic tornado farther east.

A tornado was confirmed by an induvial who picked up in a truck, rotated 120 degrees, had his windows blown out, and mirrors ripped off. He reported that the tornado was roughly the size of truck. He also reported power lines down. This was confirmed by local authorities.
Spotter reported numerous 1 to 1.5 inch hailstones.
Widespread flooded roads and other minor flooding from earlier thunderstorm activity.
Picture comparing a hailstone to a quarter, which is slightly larger.
Picture on social media, hailstones are at least as large as quarters.
Main street flooded with 1 to 2 feet of water.
Spotter reported spotting 2 funnel clouds in the tornado warned supercell west of Wiley. They also stated seeing dust kick up underneath the supercell.

A well documented strong and long lasting EF-3 tornado meandered across Prowers County south of Granada, Colorado, on June 23, 2023, remaining over open countryside for most of its life. Early during the tornadoes lifespan, it heavily impacted a family farm. Two wooden barns were completely destroyed, with little evidence |remaining of them other than the outline where they once stood. A metal farm outbuilding was virtually gone, with only the twisted steel beam reinforcements remaining. The primary family house was completely destroyed, with only a part of an interior wall still in place. After impacting the family home, the tornado continued to the southeast and knocked down power lines along County Road 25 before heading back into open countryside and dissipating.

There was also a second damaging tornado, rated EF-1, that occurred this day on June 23, 2023. This tornado drifted across mostly open rural land across far southern Baca County east of Campo, Colorado for most of its lifespan. At a point during the middle of the tornadoes life, it impacted an abandoned farm stead, damaging two structures on the property. After hitting this property, it continued to track eastward across County Road 43, where it knocked down wooden power poles. Also at this time, the tornado passed a couple hundred yards to the north of an occupied family farm, but no damage was reported at this location. After crossing County Road 43, the tornado drifted back into open countryside and began deviating to the NNE, where it eventually dissipated near County Road 45.

Heavy rainfall led to some water over short stretches of Hwy 160, county roads, ditches, and other low-lying areas. No other notable impacts reported. Radar-estimated rainfall of 1.5-2.0 inches occurred over impacted areas within warning area.

Heavy rainfall resulted in flooded roadways, including numerous on/off ramps for I-25, through central and north Pueblo. Some mud and debris accumulation also occurred on impacted roadways. Few stranded vehicles but no reported injuries or fatalities. Radar-estimated rainfall of 1.5-2.5 inches occurred within warning area.

Received call from Mykel Kroll, Fremont County Emergency Manager, notifying us of some minor flooding occurring along the Arkansas River in Florence from an ice jam downstream. Inundation of low-lying areas mostly occurred between the river and County Rd 119 in the town of Florence. No other impacts reported.

Sustained high flow releases from Pueblo Reservoir resulted in minor river flooding along the Arkansas River near Avondale, CO (ADLC2). The ADLC2 stream gauge recorded a crest of 8.97 ft, occurring on June 10, and remained above Minor Flood Stage until June 17. Minor inundation of low-lying areas and riparian zone occurred.

The Arkansas River in Ca��on City (CNCC2) fluctuated just above and below Minor Flood Stage for a couple days due to a combination of accelerated snowmelt runoff in the upper Arkansas River Basin and from sustained high flow releases from Turquoise Lake and Twin Lakes. The CNCC2 stream gauge recorded crests of 10.02 ft on two occasions from June 10 through 11.

Sustained high flow releases from Pueblo Reservoir led to some minor flooding on the Arkansas River upstream of Pueblo (PDAC2). The peak release of around 6000 cfs led to a river crest of 8.29 ft on June 10.

Sustained high flow releases from Pueblo Reservoir led to brief periods of minor flooding along the Arkansas River in La Junta (LXHC2) from June 12-13 and again on June 15. The LXHC2 stream gauge reported the first crest of 11.36 ft on June 12 and a second crest of 11.32 ft on June 15. One fatality was reported for the June 15 event.

Standing and flowing water at the RV Park and nearby roads, Oak Place and Manitou Avenue. Flash flood alert sirens and preemptive evacuations were made for local gov't facilities and RV campground along Fountain Creek. Quick rises were observed along Fountain and Ruxton Creeks, but streams remained within their banks.

The initial front of the storm brought sustained winds of approximately 75 mph, confirmed via Kestrel measurement. These winds were accompanied by a torrential downpour in Colorado City, resulting in rapid flooding in the immediate area. The initial downpour lasted approximately 45 minutes and produced street and highway flooding, with standing and moving water measured at approximately 3-5 inches in most areas, generally still traversable by passenger vehicles. Approximately 15 minutes after the rain began to lessen, reports of flooding were received for Interstate 25 at Milepost 77 and Milepost 70. Milepost 70: Flooding slowed traffic but did not result in any reported traffic accidents.  Milepost 77: Flooding rendered the interstate temporarily impassable to most vehicles, with large debris present on the roadway and several traffic accidents reported. Within approximately two hours after the storm passed, water had fully receded from all roadways, and no further significant closures or incidents were reported.

Video footage provided by Pueblo County EM and Beulah Fire Chief of swift, ash-laden stream flows, excess surface runoff and debris flows after heavy rainfall hit the eastern edge of the Oak Ridge burn scar. Some forest road, culvert and stream crossing washouts occurred from debris flows and surface runoff a few miles northwest of Beulah.

Heavy rainfall over Medano Pass, in Great Sand Dunes National Park, triggered flash flooding and debris flows along Medano Pass Primitive Road. Sections of the road, culverts and other drainage infrastructure were washed out or covered in debris.

events.event_narrative: A short-lived tornado caused no known damage in open country.

This tornado formed at 1735 MST in Crowley County, 8.1 miles east-southeast of Sugar City, and moved east for around 0.8 miles before exiting Crowley County around 8.9 miles east-southeast of Sugar City at 1736 MST. The tornado continued in Otero County for another 0.35 miles, before dissipating at 1737 MST.
A short-lived tornado knocked down part of a diseased tree and moved over open fields before dissipating.
A short-lived tornado caused no damage in open county.
A brief, weak funnel cloud occurred which stayed well above the ground.
I-25 frontage road and County Road 42 flooded.
Two and one half feet of water covered a low spot on Mesa Road.
There was water up to car windows at the intersection of South Walnut and West Cucharras.
A tornado occurred over open country and caused no damage.

A tornado formed in Bent County at 1755 MST, 21.3 miles north-northwest of Pritchett, and move south-southwest for 1.3 miles to the county line at 1757 MST, 20 miles north-northwest of Pritchett. The tornado continued moving south-southwest in Baca County for another 2.3 miles, and dissipated at 1801 MST.  There was no known damage.
Many vehicles damaged on highway 287.
Five power poles were snapped off at the bases along highway 287...and around 20 powerpoles were taken down on County Road 35.
A section of the El Paso County Courthouse roof was peeled off and a contractor worker was slightly injured.  Power to 1300 customers was lost for a short time.
A few pine trees were snapped off.
Also...winds estimated around 55 MPH with this thunderstorm...causing 3 inch diameter limbs to be broken.
House windows broken.
The city of Pueblo was particularly hard hit with golf ball to tennis ball size hail. Damage estimates were around $110 million to vehicles, structures, and crops.
A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rain that resulted in widespread street flooding across Canon City.
A thunderstorm produced intense rainfall which caused flash flooding and a mudslide just east of Fort Garland, closing or restricting travel on US Highway 160 for over two hours.
Street flooding was observed, with water depth up to the bottom of pickup truck doors.
Water 8 to 10 inches deep was noted at the intersection of Tutt and Constitution.
Creek went out of its bank and flowed across the intersection of Galley Road and San Miguel Road.
Several roads and streets were closed in Canon City, with some water around 2 1/2 feet deep.
Six inches of water was observed flowing over roadways...with several gravel roads washed out and impassable.

A tornado formed in Crowley County at 1735 MST, 8.1 miles east-southeast of Sugar City and moved into Otero County 8.9 miles east-southeast of Sugar City, or  6.5 miles north of Cheraw at 1736 MST. The tornado traveled another 0.35 miles to the east and dissipated at 1737 MST, 9.25 miles east-southeast of Sugar City, or 6.4 miles north of Cheraw.

A tornado formed in Bent County at 1755 MST, 21.3 miles north-northwest of Pritchett, and move south-southwest for 1.3 miles to the county line at 1757 MST, 20 miles north-northwest of Pritchett. The tornado continued moving south-southwest in Baca County for another 2.3 miles, and dissipated 18.3 miles north-northwest of Pritchett at 1801 MST.  There was no known damage.
A tornado formed approximately 8 miles west of Pritchett and moved south-southwest, and lasted for a brief time before dissipating.  The landspout caused no damage.

County Road 27, north of Texas Creek, had several washouts.  Fourteen people and their vehicles were stranded on the road, which leads to a popular recreation area. Washouts were as deep as 8 feet.  In addition, dirt and rock debris washed into the Arkansas River which needed to be excavated from bridge abutements.
A very weak, short-lived funnel cloud quickly dissipated.
Two boats sank as a result of 6 foot waves due to outflow winds from thunderstorms in El Paso County.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain which caused deep water over roadways and washouts.
A brief tornado occurred and caused no known damage east of Interstate 25 over open country.
A landspout moved westward through open fields just south of County Road J, and caused no damage.
A roof was partially ripped off a storage barn.
Windows broken out in the house and vehicle.
The San Luis Peoples Ditch had two breaches, flooding two properties.  Some house experience flooding of basements and crawl spaces.  Several county roads were washed out.

events.event_narrative: Heavy rain produced flowing water on streets between 6 and 12 inches in depth from the Air Force Academy through western sections of Colorado Springs.
Heavy rain caused flooding of low areas and roadways to depths of greater than six inches.  No structures were threatened.
County Road 387 was briefly closed due to debris on the road in eight different areas.
A large funnel cloud occurred.  Close up eyewitnesses reported they did not see a dust whirl on the ground.
The brief mesocyclone tornado occurred at 11,300 feet ASL.  It snapped off and uprooted dozens of conifers as moved northwest and crossed Forest Road 369.
Trees and tree limbs down, causing damage to power lines, structures and vehicles.  Two people sustained very minor injuries.
Three quarters of a mile of power poles were snapped off.
One half mile of pivot irrigation was damaged and destroyed, and a roof was partially lifted off a barn.
Two power poles were downed by thunderstorm winds.
A tornado, at one time multiple-vortex, did some damage to fencing as it moved mainly across open fields around 3 miles west of Walsh and crossed US Highway 160.

events.event_narrative: Th underpass at US Highway 287 and State Highway 96 was flooded with over 2 feet of water.  County Road 40 was also flooded.
A flash flood and mud flow on US Highway 285 near Johnson Village made the road impassible for a time.

A flash flood caused significant rises in Hayden, Wolf, Cottonwood, Butter, and Little Cottonwood Creeks.  A campground resort on County Road 6 was evacuated.  Some outbuildings took on water, but no residences were flooded.  County Roads in and around the burn scar sustained some damage.  There were no injuries.
Street flooding with water well over 6 inches deep occurred in downtown Security and a small area around.
County Road 162 was closed when over a foot of water and mud flowed through the low water crossing.
Severe wet microbursts uprooted trees.  No major damage was reported to structures or power lines.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding of County Road 11 and properties in the vicinity.  The road sustained only minor damage and was quickly repaired.
Wind driven, large hail broke windows and destroyed crops in and around Higbee.
A few trees were snapped off and uprooted.
Another round of rain caused flash flooding northwest of Cripple Creek on County Road 11.  No major road damage was reported.
Very heavy rain from a thunderstorm produced water in excess of 6 inches on streets in Las Animas and briefly flooded county roads near and south of John Martin Reservoir.
A few trees and many tree limbs were downed in Las Animas.
A strong storm produced heavy rain that flooded county roads south of Peyton and Calhan.  No major road damage was reported.
A strong storm produced heavy rain that flooded city streets and county roads to depths in excess of 6 inches from southeast Pueblo into Blende.

A significant flash flood occurred on the Junkins burn scar when a small, but intense storm moved down the South Hardscrabble watershed. Rainfall estimates of 1.5 to 2 inches caused major erosion in the canyon and piled tree and rock debris on County Road 386. The wave of water and debris moved into Greenwood and Wetmore. Remarkably, only a few outbuildings and barns were affected by water and mud as the dangerous flood waters moved through that area. County Roads remained mainly intact.

Strong storms produced brief flash flooding in and around Penrose and Florence.  In addition, significant flood waters from the Junkins burn scar swiftly moved down Hardscrabble Creek down from Wetmore causing out of channel flooding to agricultural areas.  No major damage was reported.
A strong storm produced flash flooding of county roads south of Starkville, with more than 6 inches of rushing water causing minor erosion.

A shower that fell into relatively dry air, created a damaging microburst that struck the North Shore Marina on the Pueblo Reservoir.  Damage was done to several docks and minor damage occurred to boats.
A portion of Dinkle Ditch Road was washed out at the confluence of Butter and Cottonwood Creeks.  In addition, high water flows and flash flooding also occurred along portions of Hayden Creek.
Flash flooding was noted on County Road 11, where flowing water was more than six inches deep and 100 feet wide for a time.
Wind-driven hail broke windows of vehicles and houses.
Driveways along North Creek Road were impacted with high, fast-flowing water, although the adjacent North Creek Road was not flooded.
Two modular homes were damaged, one being fiipped on its side.  They were unoccupied and no one was injured.
Lightning struck a house, causing a fire.  All family members escaped without injury.
The two brief landspouts caused no known damage from which the NWS could assign an EF-scale rating.

The tornado then lifted and traveled three-quarters of a mile to the southeast side skirting a primary residence off Elbert Road. Damage from the RV Storage facility was laying in the yard of the effected residence. The residence had one of it's exterior walls blown outward as wind got into the house through a set of french doors on the north-northwest side of the house. The remainder of the house was unaffected by the storm which then traveled a little farther southeast before dissipating.
